creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Filter banks
Multirate signal processing
Polyphase filters
Cosine-modulated filter banks
Decimation
Subband decomposition
dublinCore.description: An M-channel cosine-modulated (pseudo-QMF) filter bank built from one Hamming-windowed-sinc prototype. Shows the magnitude response of every channel, the subband energies of a multi-tone, chirp or single-tone test signal, the analysis-synthesis reconstruction error in dB, the overall response and worst alias term, and the polyphase split of the prototype with the multiplications per output sample for direct and polyphase decimation.
relation: Chapter 10: Advanced Filter Design and Implementation

learningObjectives: Calculate the edges k fs/2M and centre (2k+1) fs/4M of every channel and predict which channel or channels a tone falls into
Explain why the subband energies add up to the input energy when neighbouring channels cross at -3 dB, and to less when they cross at -6 dB
Analyze how the prototype length N and the cutoff tuning change the overall response |T|, the worst alias term and the reconstruction error
Decompose a prototype filter into its M polyphase components E_m[q] = p[qM + m] and state their length N/M
Calculate the multiplications per output sample for direct and polyphase decimation and explain where the factor M comes from
prerequisites: FIR filters, windowed-sinc design and magnitude responses in dB
Modulation by a cosine shifts a spectrum

misconceptions.misconception: Splitting a signal into M decimated subbands throws information away
misconceptions.correction: A critically sampled bank keeps M subbands at fs/M each, as many samples as the input, and the synthesis bank cancels the aliasing between neighbouring channels
misconceptions.evidence: With M = 4, N = 64, the tuned cutoff and the multi-tone input, the output matches the input to -62.0 dB

misconceptions.misconception: A polyphase filter is a different filter from the original
misconceptions.correction: The polyphase components are the prototype's taps dealt out in turn; the polyphase decimator performs the same multiplications for every kept output and skips only the outputs that downsampling discards
misconceptions.evidence: The coloured taps of p[n] reappear unchanged in E_0 ... E_M-1, and the cost read-out drops from N M to N multiplications per output sample

accessibility.screenReaderScript: An M-channel cosine-modulated filter bank. The upper left plot shows the magnitude response of every channel in its own colour above a strip with the overall analysis-synthesis response; the upper right bars show how much of the test signal energy lands in each subband. The lower left panel splits the prototype filter into M polyphase components drawn in different colours, and the lower right panel compares the input with the reconstructed signal and shows the error. Read-outs give the reconstruction error in dB and the multiplications per output sample for direct and polyphase decimation.

colorScheme.phases: viridis ramp, one colour per polyphase component m

controls.label: Channels M
controls.description: Number of channels of the filter bank, which is also the decimation factor of every subband

controls.label: Prototype length N
controls.description: Number of taps of the Hamming-windowed-sinc prototype p[n]; every channel filter has the same length

controls.label: Test signal
controls.description: Chooses four tones (0.3, 1.0, 2.3, 3.4 kHz), a linear chirp from 0 to 4 kHz, or a single tone

controls.label: Tone
controls.description: Frequency of the single-tone test signal (enabled only when single tone is selected)

controls.label: Tuned cutoff
controls.description: When checked the prototype cutoff is found by bisection so that |P| = -3 dB at pi/2M and neighbouring channels are power complementary; when unchecked the cutoff is pi/2M (-6 dB crossover)

visualElements.description: Magnitude responses |H_k| in dB of all M analysis filters, with channel numbers, band edges and test-signal frequencies, above a strip with the overall analysis-synthesis response |T| in dB
Bar chart of the test-signal energy in each subband in dB of the input energy, with their sum in percent
Stem plot of the prototype p[n] coloured by phase n mod M, and M small stem plots of the polyphase components E_m[q] = p[qM + m]
8 ms of the input and the delay-compensated reconstruction, with the reconstruction error on a magnified scale
Prototype cutoff and band-edge gain, reconstruction error in dB, range of |T|, worst alias term, and multiplications per output and per input sample for direct and polyphase decimation

model.description: A 2048-sample record at 8 kHz (with 256 samples of padding on each side) is filtered by M cosine-modulated analysis filters, each output is kept at every M-th sample, and the subbands are upsampled, filtered by the matching synthesis filters and summed. The error compares the output, delayed by N - 1, with the input. Frequency responses, the overall response T and the alias terms A_l are computed with a 2048-point radix-2 FFT.
equations: p[n] = Hamming-windowed sinc with cutoff w_c, sum p[n] = 1
x_hat[n] = sum_k sum_m v_k[m] f_k[n - mM]
T(z) = (1/M) sum_k F_k(z) H_k(z); A_l(z) = (1/M) sum_k F_k(z) H_k(z W^l), W = exp(-j 2 pi / M)
E = 10 log10( sum (x_hat[n + N - 1] - x[n])^2 / sum x[n]^2 )
multiplications per output sample: direct N M, polyphase N
algorithms: Bisection on the cutoff for a -3 dB band-edge gain
Direct convolution with decimation and expansion
limitations: The tuned windowed-sinc prototype is only approximately power complementary, so |T| keeps a ripple of up to about 0.1 dB and the reconstruction error levels off near -45 to -65 dB
For M = 8 and N = 16 the prototype cannot reach -3 dB at pi/2M; the sketch then keeps the cutoff at pi/2M and says so
Subband energies are measured on the full-rate channel outputs, before decimation

instructionalStrategies: Predict the subband energies from the tone powers, then check the bars
Toggle the cutoff tuning with a tone on a band edge
Tabulate error and worst alias term against prototype length
extensions: Add a Kaiser window or an optimized prototype and compare the error floor
Show the 2M-branch polyphase plus cosine-matrix structure that computes all M channels for about N/M + 2M multiplications per input sample
